newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia sowing up, may reverse 5-yr trend.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia sowing up, may reverse 5-yr trend.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN TOTAL GRAIN PLANTINGS MAY INCREASE SLIGHTLY
MOSCOW, June 2 - At this stage, SovEcon expects Russia's total area sown to spring grains to rise to 40.5-41.5 million hectares, up 1.0-1.5 million hectares on last year's level.
Combined with winter grain sowings, the total grain area sown for the 1997 harvest is forecast at 53.5-54.5 million hectares, compared to 53.7 million hectares last year.
The numbers mean that a five-year downward trend in Russia's grain acreage may finally reverse this year.
Assuming normal crop development, SovEcon's forecast for Russia's total grain output is still tentatively in the range of 70-75 million tonnes (1996: 69.3 million tonnes).
In the European part of Russia, the spring sowing campaign is nearly complete.

Cool weather in May slowed down planting progress in the Western and Northern regions. However, most of the grain surplus-producing regions (the Black Earth, Northern Caucasus and Povolzhsk) have completed sowing on time.
In the Urals, after some delay in mid-May due to cold weather, farmers have nearly caught up with last year's pace.
In Western Siberia, good weather continues to favour sowing.
Western Siberia and Povolzhsk mainly account for the increase in spring grain plantings (Table 2).
